extracted.intended_audience: proofreaders, copyeditors, editorial staff, typesetters, and authors preparing manuscripts for publication (University of Chicago Press style users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for proofreading, copy preparation, and style/typographic conventions for publishing (capitalization, italics, punctuation, hyphenation, numbering, indexing, proofs handling, etc.). Intended to guide production and quality control of printed matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the rules for typographic treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Be supposed to know the rules without your telling him; for instance, what titles are to be set in italics, and what be roman-quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorize and apply the house rules for when to italicize titles, when to set them in roman (roman-quote), and other typographic conventions so authors/colleagues need not be told each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate transfer of proofreader marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful in transferring marks. A mark in the wrong place means two errors uncorrected in place of one corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer proofreader marks with precision: misplacement can multiply errors. Double-check locations when applying or transcribing marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and neat arrangement when sending proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: In sending out proofs, see that everything is there. Arrange the copy and proof-sheets neatly and consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify all pages and materials accompany the proofs and organize them in order before mailing or dispatching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult job ticket before first proof dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Never send out proofs, for the first time, without consulting the job ticket for the number wanted, and the name and address of the person to whom they are to be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the job ticket to confirm the required number of proofs and the recipient's contact details before initial mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript-to-proof pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should accompany the galley-proof; the foul proof (author's marked galley-proof) should accompany the page-proof. In case no galley-proof has been sent, the manuscript should accompany the page-proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct pairing of manuscript and proof types at each stage (galley, foul, page) to preserve context for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label envelope contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate in the lower left-hand corner the contents of all the envelopes you address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the envelope contents in the lower-left corner to make handling and filing easier for recipient and production staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper fastening of proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Fasten your pins in the center at the top, not diagonally in the left-hand corner, thus covering up the directions, etc., often written there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use center-top fastening to avoid obscuring written directions and to allow safe paging and reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return reference volumes daily
rubrics_metrics.description: Return every evening to the file or the bookcase any volume that may have been taken out for reference during the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain shared reference availability by returning consulted works to their proper place each day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain neat, orderly proofroom and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that you are the housekeeper of the proof-room, and take pride in its neat and orderly appearance. Keeping the records, files, etc., naturally devolves upon you. Perfect your system so that everything can be located at a moment's notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize files and records proactively; performing housekeeping duties without being asked increases appreciation and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's marks (symbol-action mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of standard proofreader's marks with meanings (e.g., Put in SMALL CAPITALS; Put in lower case; Put in italics; Put in bold face type; Dele (delete); Letter reversed — turn; Indent, make a new paragraph; Put in space; Close up — no space; Bad spacing — space more evenly; Wrong font; Transpose; Carry to the left/right; Elevate/Depress; Perfect letter — correct; Space shows between words — shove down; Straighten crooked line; Restore or retain words crossed out; Print as a logotype; Words omitted — out-set copy; Query to author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standardized marks to communicate typographic and textual corrections unambiguously; when in doubt, query the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Italics: defined and rules for use (need not be used in lengthy bibliographical lists); rules include italics for titles of books and other works, words and phrases from foreign languages, emphasis, letters designating unknown quantities, names of genera and species, names of planets/constellations/stars, symbols indicating subdivisions, titles after signatures, and continuation words like 'continued'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow section 58–73 (as referenced) for precise situations requiring italicizing; avoid italics in long bibliographies unless specified; use for emphasis and specific technical or nomenclatural items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small caps and capitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitals: rules for use, capitals and small capitals; how indicated and rules for use of small capitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply capitalization rules (sections 1–57) and small-cap conventions (50–51); indicate typographically as prescribed (257).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules (general and specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization: detailed rules for capitalization of numerous categories (proper nouns, titles, academic degrees, organizations, historical epochs and events, geographic names, governmental bodies, books of Bible, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the enumerated rules (1–57 and many topic-specific entries) to decide capitalization in each context; consult the relevant numbered section for edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and hyphenation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphens: rules for use of, hyphenization rules (182–214), hyphenated words list, compounds formation and treatment with prefixes and specific elements (co-, pre-, re-, extra-, infra-, super-, non-, bi-, tri-, semi-, vice-, ex-, elect, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rules 182–214 for forming compounds, indicating divisional hyphens, and hyphen use in fractions and other constructions; consult lists for common hyphenated forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comma: definition and illustrations of use; many rules including omission between two adjectives, use after digits for thousands, before conjunctions, with appositional, parenthetical, participial, adverbial clauses, to separate identical words, numbers, proper nouns, etc. (rules 141–162).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the detailed comma rules in sections 141–162; observe exceptions (e.g., omission in signatures) and special list cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Colon: definition and illustration of use; rules for use (131–36) including after salutatory phrases in letters, between place and publisher, to introduce extracts, to emphasize close connection between clauses, to introduce statements or enumerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colon to introduce material closely related or to emphasize a following clause or list; follow section 131–136 for specific constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes and their uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Dashes: definition and illustrations of use; different sizes explained; rules for use (166–75) including indicating pause, transition, emphasis, connection of numbers, break or change in sentence, preceding summarizing clauses, use with parenthetical and complementary clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate dash (en/em) for context; use per rules to denote pauses, ranges, or emphasis; see 166–175 for specifics such as dash for 'to' in time-indications and en-dash use between page ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and brackets usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses: rules for use (176–77); use parentheses for parenthetical clauses and figures/letters indicating subsections; within parentheses use brackets for interpolations and explanations (178).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parentheses for subsidiary material and brackets for material inside parentheses or editorial interpolations; follow section 176–179 for punctuation and nesting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses usage in quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipses: rules for use (180–81); to be treated as part of the quotation; use to indicate omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat ellipsis as part of quoted material per specified rules; use consistently to indicate omitted text in quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations and citation handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations: rules for reduction of quotations (85–87); citations from different authors following each other; punctuation of citations; handling passages in author's own words (74).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce and punctuate quotations according to the manual's rules; when consecutive citations from different authors appear, format as instructed in the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers: rules for when to spell out vs use figures (e.g., commence a sentence spelled out, less-than-three-digits spelled out in ordinary reading-matter, groups of six or more set in figures). Use of comma for thousands, dash for ranges, en-dash for consecutive pages; numerals (Arabic/Roman) spacing at line starts/headlines (271).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply numeric rules in sections 94–96, 154, 159, 171–173; be consistent across connected numeric groups and use punctuation (comma/dash/en-dash) per prescribed contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates: omit 'st/nd/rd/th' in dates, use of comma between month and year, hundreds repeated in dates when/when not (173), and relation of dates to volume numbers in references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format dates without ordinal suffixes; follow guidance on comma usage and repeating hundreds; consult bibliography/reference sections for publication dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes style and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes: general style for footnotes, numbering, placing of index figure, rules 232–39; indices for references to footnotes and sequence of indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and place footnote markers as specified; use the prescribed order and symbols for footnote indices and consult exceptions for particular journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing rules and treatment of names/particles
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing: rules for indexing (240); treatment of prefixes/particles in proper nouns, italicizing 'See'/'See also' in cross-references, and rules for alphabetizing names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the indexing rules for particle handling and cross-reference formatting; ensure consistent alphabetization per section 240.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and headlines formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings: described (279–83); headlines spacing, omission of period after headlines, and 'continued' to be set in italics when following headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set headings according to the manual's levels and typographic rules; avoid periods after headlines unless directed; use 'continued' in italics when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables/figures: columns of figures spacing and use of leaders (244–45); open tables headlines, how to set tables and specimens, use of double rules in tables, and letters referring to parts of illustrations (68, 241, 247).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format tables with proper spacing, leaders, rules, and headlines per sections 241–249; label figure parts and references consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words and hyphenation in typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of words: rules for division (215–31), systems of division, avoidance of unnecessary division, not dividing certain letters, and use of hyphen to indicate division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bad breaks; follow the prescribed division systems and hyphen-placement rules, and avoid dividing short or problematic digraphs/letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italicize scientific and foreign nomenclature appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Italicizing: names of genera and species, astronomical names, letters designating unknown quantities, and foreign words; retention of accents in foreign words incorporated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use italics for biological/astronomical terms and foreign words per sections 59–71; retain diacritics as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of abbreviations and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations: rules for abbreviations in literary references (no), spacing of elements of certain abbreviations, omission of periods after initials or abbreviations in some cases, lists of abbreviations for biblical books, treatment of metric and chemical symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the enumerated rules (106–123 and notes) for when to use periods/spaces with abbreviations and when to omit punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic degrees and titles capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic degrees: abbreviation and capitalization rules for degrees and civil/military/honorary titles (sections cited include 21–22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize and abbreviate degrees and titles per the specific rules; treat institutional officers and titles according to the University-of-Chicago-specific conventions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing rules and even spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Even spacing: importance of even spacing, hair-spacing tabooed, definitions of em/en/quad spaces and their use; spacing of numerals, mathematical formulae, and symbols (259–273).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent spacing (avoid hair-spacing), use proper em/en/quads as defined, and follow spacing rules for numerals/formulae as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign words and English equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign languages: English equivalent of foreign word/phrase to be quoted, sentences and passages quoted from foreign languages, and words from foreign languages to be italicized; translations accompany cited foreign language material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When quoting foreign-language material, provide English equivalents as quoted or translated per section 78 and follow italicization and punctuation rules for foreign words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of juridical/legislative documents and names
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts, bills, laws, juridical acts: capitalization of names of acts, bills, laws, and capitalization/treatment of names of legislative/judiciary/administrative bodies (18 and 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize legal instrument titles and governmental bodies according to the rules; consult the legal-forms section for citation format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type conventions: face, font, and display indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Face/font definitions, bold-face type how indicated, centering and display head conventions, and how to indicate type changes (e.g., small caps, nonroman faces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply typographic conventions (face, font, bold, small caps) as defined and indicated; mark changes clearly for compositors and typesetters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote index symbols and their order
rubrics_metrics.description: Indices for footnote references: symbols to be used (asterisk, dagger, double dagger, parallel mark, paragraph mark), how to number and place index figures, and sequence rules (232, 236, 240).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed symbol sequence for nonnumeric footnotes and follow placement conventions for index figures; consult journal exceptions when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic reference conventions (ibid., op. cit., loc. cit.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic references: use of ibid., loc. cit., op. cit., form of footnotes for periodicals and journals (samples and exceptions), placing page symbols, and rules for references to periodicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format references using the manual's prescribed abbreviations and placement rules; consult the samples for discipline/journal-specific exceptions.
